rationale.conceptual: The method relies on established DFT techniques (GGA-PBE, DFT-D2, COSMO solvent model, LST/QST) but demands careful implementation of multiple interacting components (structure preparation, total energy calculations under different conditions, transition state search). Understanding the underlying physics is necessary to choose correct protocols.
rationale.execution: The workflow comprises several sequential stages: optimization of the monolayer and isolated clusters, repeated geometry optimizations for six adsorbates under four condition pairs each, and a transition state search. Managing numerous DFT jobs, handling energy extraction, and ensuring correct input parameters require non-trivial scripting and pipeline orchestration.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires carrying out a standard first-principles workflow (adsorption energies with and without vdW, in vacuum and implicit solvent, plus a transition-state diffusion barrier) using DFT. The method is non-trivial but well-known in computational chemistry; the pipeline involves many individual calculations that must be correctly set up and executed.

compute_estimate.reasoning: The 2x2 InP3 supercell (~32 atoms) plus adsorbates with standard GGA-PBE plane-wave DFT fits on a single multi-core CPU with modest memory (few GB); no large datasets are needed.
